title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA1LD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1RC1RA_1RD0RF_0LE---_1LA1LE_0RA1LD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The run is a sequence of epochs. Within an epoch a bouncer grows (011)^a (101)^3 (01)^b at the left end at fixed rates; at the end of an epoch the blocks are emptied into an irregular region that holds the rest of the tape and grows from epoch to epoch (about 1,600 compressed words at 4·108 steps, 5,000 at 1.7·109). Measured, not proved. Halting needs D on a 1, entered from C on a 0 or F on a 1; never one step away in the first 3·106 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 48,325 cells have been visited and 29,619 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.554). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.309).

claims.title: Shift rules of the sweeps
claims.text: Lean proves, for every count and every tape around, the shift rules: A crosses (100)^n leftward turning it into (110)^n (5 steps per copy), and A crosses (01)^n rightward turning it into (11)^n (2 steps per copy).

claims.title: Epochs of steady growth
claims.text: At the head's visits to the left end (C there) the tape starts C>0 (011)^a (101)^3 (01)^b …, and within an epoch every 400 visits add 200 to a and 600 to b: (1131, 221) at step 403,575,993, (1331, 821), (1531, 1421), …, (4531, 10421) at step 857,064,593. The rest of the tape does not change during the epoch.

claims.title: Epoch ends feed an irregular region
claims.text: An epoch ends with a long pass that empties the blocks; afterwards a and b start small again and the irregular region on the right is larger: about 500 compressed words before the epoch that ends between 3.1 and 4.0·10<sup>8</sup> steps, 1,581 after it; 5,017 after the one that ends between 8.6·10<sup>8</sup> and 1.7·10<sup>9</sup>. Epochs get longer (they end between 1.1 and 1.6·10<sup>8</sup>, between 3.1 and 4.0·10<sup>8</sup>, between 8.6·10<sup>8</sup> and 1.7·10<sup>9</sup>, and none from 1.7·10<sup>9</sup> to 2·10<sup>9</sup>).

claims.title: Never one step from a halt
claims.text: The machine halts when D reads a 1; D is entered from C reading a 0 (C0 → 1RD) and from F reading a 1 (F1 → 1LD). In the first 3·10<sup>6</sup> steps that happens 296,494 times, and D always lands on a 0.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Inside an epoch the machine is a simple bouncer; what happens at the end of an epoch, where the blocks are poured into the irregular region, is not understood, and that region is where a halt would have to come from.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine fills two blocks at its left end at a steady rate for longer and longer epochs, and at the end of each epoch dumps them into a growing irregular region. This page shows the epochs and what is proved.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 48,325 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Steady growth within an epoch
html: Look at the tape each time the head is back at the left end (state C):
((011)^5 is 011 five times.) Every 400 visits the first block gains 200 copies and the second 600, while the rest of the tape stays the same.

sections.heading: Dumping into an irregular region
html: Then, at the end of the epoch, a long pass empties both blocks into the region to their right, which is an irregular mix of short blocks and walls. A new epoch starts with small blocks and a bigger region (about 1,600 compressed words after the epoch that ends between 3.1 and 4.0·108 steps, 5,000 after the next one). Each epoch is longer than the one before. What decides the end of an epoch, and what the dump does, is not yet understood.

sections.heading: What a halt would need
html: The machine stops only in D reading a 1. D is entered from C reading a 0 (moving right) and from F reading a 1 (moving left). In the first 3·106 steps that happens 296,494 times, and D always lands on a 0. A halt would have to come from the irregular region: open.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.554). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.309).
After 109 steps the tape spans 48,325 cells (32,009 left of the start, 4,201 right), with a density of 1s of 0.613.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: bouncer that periodically dumps into a growing irregular region
summary: A bouncer at the left end grows two blocks at fixed rates ((011) by 1 and (01) by 3 per two left visits) for an ever longer epoch; then a long pass empties them into an irregular region on the right, which grows from epoch to epoch.
